classification.difficultyReason: Sketch a supplied curve after horizontal dilation, translation and, in two parts, reflection.

Sketch the graph of the following.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 18, right column, shared given graph
spec.description: An unshaded blue arch above black arrowed axes, with endpoints (-1,0) and (1,0) and maximum (0,1).
spec.mathematics: The source gives an illustrative graph without an equation. Editable Bézier segments preserve its displayed shape and identified coordinates; they do not assert a formula for f.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent shared given; no transformed graphs appear in the question.

answer.short:
Arch with endpoints $(\tfrac32,0)$ and $(\tfrac52,0)$ and maximum $(2,1)$.

Dilate horizontally by $\tfrac12$, then translate right $2$ units.
answer.worked:
Dilate horizontally by a factor of $\tfrac12$ using $x\mapsto2x$, then translate right $2$ units using $x\mapsto x-2$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f(2x)\\y&=f\bigl(2(x-2)\bigr)\\y&=f(2x-4)\end{align*}$$
The endpoints become $(\tfrac32,0)$ and $(\tfrac52,0)$; the maximum becomes $(2,1)$. Sketch the horizontally compressed arch through these points.

spec.sourceRegion: 18(a); answer evidence teacher PDF page 70, printed page 648
spec.description: Compressed arch centred at x=2, with intercepts 3/2 and 5/2, height 1 and dashed coordinate guides.
spec.mathematics: Every point (u,v) of the given graph maps to (u/2+2,v). The editable source-shape control points undergo the same transformation.

answer.short:
Arch with endpoints $(-\tfrac52,0)$ and $(-\tfrac32,0)$ and maximum $(-2,1)$.

Dilate horizontally by $\tfrac12$, then translate left $2$ units.
answer.worked:
Dilate horizontally by a factor of $\tfrac12$ using $x\mapsto2x$, then translate left $2$ units using $x\mapsto x+2$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f(2x)\\y&=f\bigl(2(x+2)\bigr)\\y&=f(2x+4)\end{align*}$$
The endpoints become $(-\tfrac52,0)$ and $(-\tfrac32,0)$; the maximum becomes $(-2,1)$. Sketch the horizontally compressed arch through these points.

spec.sourceRegion: 18(b); answer evidence teacher PDF page 70, printed page 648
spec.description: Compressed arch centred at x=-2, with intercepts -5/2 and -3/2, height 1 and dashed coordinate guides.
spec.mathematics: Every point (u,v) maps to (u/2-2,v), including the displayed endpoints and maximum.

answer.short:
Arch with endpoints $(-\tfrac52,0)$ and $(-\tfrac32,0)$ and maximum $(-2,1)$.

Dilate horizontally by $\tfrac12$, reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate left $2$ units.
answer.worked:
Dilate horizontally by $\tfrac12$ using $x\mapsto2x$, reflect in the $y$-axis using $x\mapsto-x$, then translate left $2$ units using $x\mapsto x+2$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f(2x)\\y&=f(-2x)\\y&=f\bigl(-2(x+2)\bigr)\\y&=f(-2x-4)\end{align*}$$
The original left endpoint becomes $(-\tfrac32,0)$ and the original right endpoint becomes $(-\tfrac52,0)$. The maximum becomes $(-2,1)$. The given arch is symmetric, so the final sketch matches part (b).

spec.sourceRegion: 18(c); answer evidence teacher PDF page 70, printed page 648
spec.description: Reflected compressed arch centred at x=-2, with intercepts -5/2 and -3/2 and maximum height 1.
spec.mathematics: Every point (u,v) maps to (-u/2-2,v). Reflection exchanges the source endpoints; the symmetric shape agrees with part (b).

answer.short:
Arch with endpoints $(\tfrac32,0)$ and $(\tfrac52,0)$ and maximum $(2,1)$.

Dilate horizontally by $\tfrac12$, reflect in the $y$-axis, then translate right $2$ units.
answer.worked:
Dilate horizontally by $\tfrac12$ using $x\mapsto2x$, reflect in the $y$-axis using $x\mapsto-x$, then translate right $2$ units using $x\mapsto x-2$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=f(2x)\\y&=f(-2x)\\y&=f\bigl(-2(x-2)\bigr)\\y&=f(-2x+4)\end{align*}$$
The original left endpoint becomes $(\tfrac52,0)$ and the original right endpoint becomes $(\tfrac32,0)$. The maximum becomes $(2,1)$. The given arch is symmetric, so the final sketch matches part (a).
